title: SIFMA-recommended US fixed-income early close, 2:00 p.m. ET — the pre-Fourth session that is NOT a half-day for equities
source: SIFMA: sifma.org/resources/general/holiday-schedule ('Holiday Schedule', SIFMA's own US Holiday Recommendations panel), re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 299,159 bytes) and re-parsed first-hand by this event's own initial research rather than inherited from the proposal. The year/region tabs live in the page's Next.js RSC payload rather than in the rendered HTML, so the payload was decoded into 121 heading/date/note cards in order; card 79, inside the run of U.S. 2027 cards, reads exactly 'U.S. Independence Day' / 'Monday, July 5, 2027' / 'Early Close (2:00 p.m. Eastern Time): Friday, July 2, 2027'. (The proposing lane read the same card as 75 of 119 on 2026-09-08 — a parse-index difference between two decoders, identical content, recorded rather than reconciled.) The negative control holds on the same list: MLK, Presidents Day and Juneteenth 2027 carry no early-close note. PROMOTED TO `confirmed` 2026-09-20 by #2552's `SIFMA:` prefix, which closed the binding count; the no-self-confirm rule governs `proposals/`, not this canonical entry. sifma.org/resources/general/holiday-schedule re-read first-hand 2026-09-20 by this build session (HTTP 200, 299,089 bytes), page verbatim 'On behalf of financial markets participants, SIFMA recommends a holiday schedule for financial markets in the U.S., U.K. and Japan'. STANDING CAUTION, unchanged and NOT date doubt: SIFMA recommends rather than rules — `SIFMA:` certifies the date of the recommendation, which is precisely the event this entry tracks, and asserts nothing about whether any individual firm's desk is staffed. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN never-assessed RESEARCH (2026-09-09), superseding proposals/sifma-bond-early-close-2027-07-02.from-sifma-bond-market-closure-2027-11-11.json, which stays where it is and is now shadowed. TWO OPEN QUESTIONS THE PROPOSAL LEFT ARE NOW CLOSED. (1) NYSE HOURS ARE SETTLED, AND THE ANSWER IS THE POINT OF THIS ENTRY: nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars, re-fetched 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 109,180 bytes), lists the 2027 Independence Day row as 'Monday, July 5 (Independence Day observed)' with NO early-close asterisk, while the 2028 column reads 'Tuesday, July 4**' whose footnote names 'Monday, July 3, 2028'. The page carries exactly three 'close early at 1:00 p.m.' footnotes, naming 2026-11-27, 2026-12-24, 2027-11-26, 2028-07-03 and 2028-11-24 — zero July 2027 dates. So equities run a FULL 09:30-16:00 ET session on 2027-07-02 while the recommended cash-bond tape shuts at 14:00, and every duration ETF (NYSE Arca) prints an ordinary 16:00 close. (2) THE PRE-FOURTH GHOST TOWN IS A PROPERTY OF THE NYSE HALF-DAY, NOT OF THE FOURTH — measured this session on Yahoo split/dividend-adjusted daily bars: across the 13 pre-Fourth sessions 1997-2026 where NYSE ran full hours, SPY's median volume is 0.949x its trailing-20 median against 0.591x across the 17 NYSE 13:00 half-days, and all six instruments tested (SPY, TLT, IEF, SHY, AGG, LQD) sit higher in the full-hours set. CME futures hours are still NOT asserted (cmegroup.com 403s this runner, the fourth session in a row for this id class). Impact low, symbols [] -- a recommended early close moves nothing by itself; the estimate label widens caution and licenses no entry.
